passage:
A river in the city had an official modern name, but older residents used a different name from a local language.
Students researched both names. The older name described the sound of water over stones. The modern name came from a government map.
The class made signs showing both names and their meanings.
Residents reacted warmly. Some said they had not heard the old name written publicly for years.
The project showed that names carry power. Renaming can organize a place, but it can also cover earlier memory.
Restoring a name does not change the river's water, but it changes how people listen to it.
